source_text: II. Tunc proconsul iussit eum fustibus caedi. cumque caederetur dicebat ei: Sacrifica, Maxime, ut ab his liber sis tormentis. Maximus respondit: Haec non sunt tormenta, quae pro nomine domini nostri Iesu Christi inferuntur, sed sunt unctiones. si enim recessero a domini mei praeceptis, quibus sum de evangelio eius eruditus, vera et perpetua mihi manebunt tormenta. tunc proconsul iussit eum in equuleo suspendi. cumque torqueretur dicebat ad eum: Iam resipisce, miser, ab insipientia tua et sacrifica, ut animam lucreris. Maximus respondit: Animam meam lucrabor, si non sacrificavero; quod si sacrificavero, perdo eam. mihi enim nec fustes nec ungulae nec ignis sentiendi dant dolorem; quia in me manet gratia Christi, quae me salvum faciet in aeternum omnium sanctorum orationibus, qui in hac colluctatione certantes vestras superaverunt insanias nobisque virtutum exempla reliquerunt. tunc proconsul dedit in eum sententiam dicens: Eum qui sacris legibus assensum noluit accommodare, ut magnae deae Dianae sacrificaret, ad metum reliquorum Christianorum obrui lapidibus praecepit divina clementia.
thought_title: Beating and rack called anointing, then sentence to stoning
orientation: Maximus has confessed as a Christian before the proconsul Optimus and refused to offer sacrifice, and Optimus now has him beaten and racked.
pass_a_gloss: Then the proconsul ordered him to be beaten with clubs. And while he was being beaten he kept saying to him: Offer sacrifice, Maximus, so that you may be free from this torture. Maximus answered: These are not torture, which are inflicted for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, but they are anointing. For if I withdraw from the commands of my Lord, by which I have been taught from his gospel, true and everlasting torture will remain for me. Then the proconsul ordered him to be hung up on the rack. And while he was being tortured he kept saying to him: Now come to your senses, wretched man, from your folly and offer sacrifice, so that you may gain your soul. Maximus answered: I will gain my soul, if I do not offer sacrifice; but if I offer sacrifice, I destroy it. For neither clubs nor claws nor fire give me pain for feeling; because Christ's grace remains in me, which will make me safe forever through the prayers of all the saints, who contending in this struggle have overcome your madnesses and have left to us examples of courage. Then the proconsul gave sentence against him saying: Him who refused to give assent to the sacred laws, that he should offer sacrifice to great goddess Diana, the divine mercy has ordered to be buried with stones for the fear of the remaining Christians.

pass_b_english: Then the proconsul ordered him to be beaten with clubs. As he was being beaten, the proconsul said to him, "Offer sacrifice, Maximus, so you may be freed from this torture." Maximus answered, "What is inflicted for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ is not torture, but anointing. If I abandon the commands of my Lord, in which I have been instructed from his gospel, true and everlasting torture will await me."

Then the proconsul ordered him to be hung on the rack. While he was being tortured, he said to him, "Come to your senses now, wretch, leave your folly behind and offer sacrifice, so you may gain your soul." Maximus answered, "I will gain my soul if I do not offer sacrifice, but if I offer sacrifice I lose it. Neither clubs nor hooks nor fire cause me any felt pain, for Christ's grace remains in me, and through the prayers of all the saints it will save me forever. Those saints contended in this same struggle, overcame your madness, and left us examples of virtue."

Then the proconsul passed sentence on him, saying, "The man who has refused to assent to the sacred laws by offering sacrifice to the great goddess Diana, divine mercy has ordered to be overwhelmed with stones, to frighten the remaining Christians."
